summary.short: Commission proposal that would amend the GDPR, EUDPR, ePrivacy Directive, Data Act, NIS2, eIDAS, DORA, CER Directive and Single Digital Gateway Regulation, move the Data Governance Act, Open Data Directive and free-flow rules into the Data Act, and repeal the P2B Regulation, mostly from entry into force.
summary.long: The proposal would fold the Data Governance Act, Regulation 2018/1807 and the Open Data Directive into the Data Act as Chapters VIIa-VIIc (voluntary registration of data intermediaries and data altruism organisations, a ban on national localisation requirements for non-personal data, re-use of public sector and protected data with charging rules and higher charges for very large enterprises), create a European Data Innovation Board, narrow business-to-government data requests to public emergencies, and exempt pre-12 September 2025 custom or SME/SMC cloud contracts from switching rules. In the GDPR it adds an entity-relative test for personal data, a definition of scientific research, legitimate interest and a special-category exception for AI development and operation, an exception for biometric verification under the data subject's sole control, limits on abusive access requests and information duties, a high-risk-only 96-hour breach notification via an ENISA single-entry point, EU-wide DPIA lists, and new rules on terminal-equipment access (consent with exceptions, single-click refusal from 6 months; machine-readable signals from 24 months; browser support from 48 months), removing personal data from ePrivacy Art. 5(3). NIS2, eIDAS, DORA and CER reporting moves to the single-entry point after 18 months. The P2B Regulation is repealed, with some provisions kept until 2032.

territorial_scope.description: EU-wide regulation directly applicable in all Member States; data intermediaries and data altruism organisations without an EU establishment that seek registration must appoint an EU legal representative, and third-country access and transfer rules reach non-EU authorities and re-users.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

definitions.term: Bodies governed by public law (Data Act)

evidence.quote: 'bodies governed by public law' means bodies that have all of the following characteristics:

'public undertaking' means any undertaking over which a public sector body may exercise directly or indirectly a dominant influence by virtue of their ownership of it, their financial participation therein, or the rules which govern it.

'data intermediation service' means a service which aims to establish relationships of an economic character for the purposes of data sharing between an undetermined number of data subjects or data holders and data users

'data altruism' means the voluntary sharing of data on the basis of the consent of data subjects to process personal data pertaining to them, or of permissions of data holders to allow the use of their non-personal data without seeking or receiving a reward that goes beyond compensation
'medium-sized enterprise' means a medium-sized enterprise as defined in Article 2 of Annex I to Recommendation 2003/361/EC
'small mid-cap' or 'SMC' means a small mid-cap enterprise as defined in Article 2 of the Annex to Commission Recommendation (EU) 2025/1099
'document' means: (a) any content that is non-digital whatever its medium
'dynamic data' means data and documents in a digital form, subject to frequent or real-time updates
'research data' means data , other than scientific publications, which are collected or produced in the course of scientific research activities
're-use' means the use by natural persons or legal entities of documents held by:
'high-value datasets' means data and documents the re-use of which is associated with important benefits for society, the environment and the economy

definitions.term: Certain categories of protected data (Data Act)

evidence.quote: 'certain categories of protected data' means data and documents held by public sector bodies which are protected on the grounds of
'secure processing environment' means the physical or virtual environment and organisational means to ensure compliance with Union law
're-user' means a natural or legal person who was granted the right to re-use data or documents held by a public sector body or a public undertaking under Chapter VIIc
'reasonable return on investment' means a percentage of the overall charge, in addition to the amount needed to recover the eligible costs
'data localisation requirement' means any obligation, prohibition, condition, limit or other requirement provided for in the laws, regulations or administrative provisions of a Member State

entities.note: No firms or facilities are named. Public bodies with tasks (Commission, ENISA, EDPB, EDPS, ECB, European Data Innovation Board) are institutional addressees, not entities in the codebook sense.

notes: Proposal: obligations and thresholds describe what would apply if adopted as proposed; no later Parliament or Council text was annotated. Dates are mostly OP placeholders relative to entry into force or 'entry into application', which the text does not fix for the Data Act amendments (resolve stage). Role approximations (vocabulary gaps): Data Act 'data holder', data altruism organisations and protected-data re-users coded data_controller; providers of data processing services coded data_processor; data intermediation services providers coded data_broker; web-browser providers and eIDAS notifiers coded platform_operator; Member State duties to ensure that NIS2 essential/important entities and CER critical entities report coded government_agency. Penalties for the new GDPR/EUDPR provisions are not addressed in the text (GDPR Art. 83 is not amended or cross-referenced), so no GDPR enforcement row is coded. Removed duties: GDPR Arts. 57(1)(k), 64(1)(a), 70(1)(h) (supervisory-authority DPIA lists), ePrivacy Art. 4, Data Act Arts. 14-15, 36, 17(5)-(6), 18(5), and EUDPR Art. 39(5)-(6) are deleted. Internal inconsistencies in the text (codebook 6.8): (1) Art. 1(27) says 'Annex I is added as set out in the Annex II to this Regulation' and Art. 32u(1) refers to Annex I, but Annex II's heading refers to 'Article 32ab(1)'; (2) Art. 11 says 'Deviating from paragraph 3' though Art. 11 has no numbered paragraphs, and the ePrivacy change applies 6 months after publication rather than after entry into force; (3) the title lists the amended acts but omits Regulation (EU) 910/2014 and Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, which Arts. 7-8 amend; (4) Data Act Art. 32t(2) refers to 'Article 32n, paragraph 3, point (d)', which does not exist; (5) new Data Act Art. 2 skips points (49) and (55); the EUDPR amendments in Art. 4 renumber points as (8)-(9); (6) recital 59 cites 'Regulation (EU) 2019/1050' for the P2B Regulation (Art. 10 cites 2019/1150); (7) NIS2 Art. 23a(5) bracketed '[18] months' and the European Business Wallets title are drafting placeholders.
